facts.label: Off the beaten path, by the Training Track

sections.title: Where the riders *eat breakfast*
body: For decades the Track Kitchen has served Southern-style home cooking to the exercise riders and trainers of the Aiken Training Track when their early-morning workouts are done.
It sits off the beaten path in Aiken's horse district, and visitors who find it get breakfast and a seat among the people who keep Aiken's horses running.

items.title: Find Mead Avenue
items.text: We're at 420 Mead Avenue, beside the Aiken Training Track in the horse district.

items.title: Come early
items.text: Breakfast is built around the riders' early mornings. Call ahead for the day's hours.

items.title: Get your own coffee
items.text: Coffee is self-serve, so help yourself.

items.title: Settle in
items.text: Southern home cooking, shared with the people who ride and train Aiken's horses.

sections.title: In town for the horses?
sections.text: Start your morning where the riders do. Call for today's hours.

before: No website of its own: a search leads to a Facebook page and directory listings
Listings disagree on the hours, and some even on the street number
Visitors have to piece together how it works from travel blogs
after: A site the Track Kitchen owns, at its own address
Phone, address and map in one obvious place
One-tap call and directions on a phone
A short guide for first-time visitors
Room to add the menu, photos and hours as the owner supplies them
